newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-M.A.I.D in final global deal talks.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-M.A.I.D in final global deal talks.

text.p: M.A.I.D Plc, the UK on-line information service, said on Thursday it was in final discussion with global alliances that would allow it to sell its news and data to specific target markets.

Dan Wagner, founder and chief executive, said in an interview that having tied up International Business Machines Corp, Thorn Plc, Nokia Ab, Oy and CompuServe Corp, M.A.I.D was poised to seal new deals.
"You can expect more substantial, global alliances to be tied up with in the next few months that we've been working on for quite some time," he said.
Wagner said new partners were likely to be telecoms groups, major publishing groups and online companies that would allow M.A.I.D to reach more customers.
M.A.I.D earlier sent its share jumping in relief after fourth quarter and final figures pointed to a turnaround of the group's fortunes and a promise of profitability in 1997.
Heavy invesments in the year had started to pay off, Wagner said, as third quarter losses of 2.4 million stg were reduced to 1.4 million in the fourth with a 29 percent rise in sales.
Full year pretax losses came in at 7.03 million stg as turnover jumped 57 percent to 21.4 million stg.

"We have now stabilised our costs against the background of continued increasing revenues in both the core business and through alliance relationships," he said. "We are well positioned for profitable growth in 1997 and beyond."

Wagner said the group, which this month partnered with the Hong Kong-based South China Morning Post newspaper to design and implement its Internet business service, was putting its markers down in all the different areas required to build a long-term position in the future of electronic publishing.
About 70 percent of services offered by M.A.I.D, which said corporate customers had trebled from 1,200 to 3,800, are based on research data.
But the group also provides real-time news with its LiveWire services, which allows users to be alerted to pre-selected, requested headlines as they appear on M.A.I.D software.

Personalised access to 27 live feeds, ranging from the UK regulatory stock exchange wire to U.S. news agency Associated Press costs 150 pounds per month for 20 desks, Wagner said, undercutting rival services by news and information services Reuters Holdings Plc and U.S. new agency Bloomberg.
The deal with Nokia allows users to access share price and foreign exchange information on hand-held devises and Intranet television deals allows the services into hotel rooms.
M.A.I.D says because its electronic services are mainly research, rather than news, it is not threatened by companies providing news directly on websites.
"Ours is a supermarket of intelligence," Wagner said. "News is one element our of brokerage research, country and economic research, market research, company research.
"The threat of the Internet is non-existent, the opportunity is enormous."
